section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the date and heading for the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Wednesday,
the fifteenth of Av, 5735*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions the comparison between the joy of the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur, and why this teaching concludes Tractate Ta'anis.
section.t: There were no better days for Israel than the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur,
and it is necessary to understand what is the reason for the similarity and the common denominator between the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur.
Also, it is necessary to understand that this statement
("There were no better days etc.")
is at the conclusion and seal
of Tractate Ta'anis,
and yet festivals are a matter of joy,
the opposite of the matter of fasting.
And especially, from the language "There were no better days for Israel than the fifteenth of Av etc." it is evident that the joy of the fifteenth of Av
(and Yom Kippur)
is greater than the joy of a festival, even though it is a positive commandment from the Torah,
"And you shall rejoice in your festival,"
and according to this, the connection of this matter to
(the conclusion and seal)
of Tractate Ta'anis specifically is even more difficult.
Now, the connection of the fifteenth of Av to the matter of fasting is also evident from the fact that it links
(in the Mishnah)
the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur,
for Yom Kippur is the only fast day from the Torah,
and this fast is unique and different from other fasts also in that the four fasts
(and also the fasts enumerated in Megillas Taanis,
and several of them are brought in the Tur)
will be turned into joy and gladness,
but this is not the case regarding the fast of Yom Kippur, which will remain even in the future.
And from this that it links
(in the Mishnah)
the fifteenth of Av with Yom Kippur,
it is evident
that the festival of the fifteenth of Av is related not only to the matter of fasting in Tractate Ta'anis
[therefore the statement "There were no better days for Israel than the fifteenth of Av" is at the conclusion and seal of Tractate Ta'anis],
but also to the fast of Yom Kippur.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the joy of the fifteenth of Av relates to the weakening of the sun's power, which parallels Yom Kippur's atonement through human service.
section.t: Now, the reason why the fifteenth of Av is a festival
[for superficially it is not understood,
and as the Gemara asks:
Granted, Yom Kippur, because it has forgiveness and pardon,
the day on which the latter tablets were given,
but the fifteenth of Av, what is it?],
is brought in the discourses
from the Pri Etz Chaim,
because then is the filling of the moon.
And it questions this in the discourses,
but every month has a fifteenth day
(when it is the filling of the moon),
and what is the superiority of the fifteenth of Av specifically,
and from what is said "There were no better days etc. like the fifteenth of Av" it implies that it is superior even to the fifteenth of Nissan
(Pesach)
and the fifteenth of Tishrei
(Sukkos).
Now, one of the reasons in the Gemara there
(for why the fifteenth of Av is a festival)
is,
because then the power of the sun weakened.
And it is not understood,
the weakening of the sun's power is a matter in the heavenly luminaries and does not pertain to man's affairs and actions
(like the other reasons in the Gemara there),
and if so, what is the festival when the sun's power weakened?
And although from this that the sun's power weakened
(even though it is a matter in the heavenly luminaries)
there are consequences regarding matters and actions on earth,
and as it states in the Gemara there, "and they would not cut wood for the arrangement etc.,"
nevertheless, from the language of the Gemara
("From the fifteenth of Av and onward the power of the sun weakened")
it implies that the festival
(and the joy)
of the fifteenth of Av is because of this very thing, that the power of the sun weakened
(and not only because of the consequences brought about by this),
and if so, it must be said,
that this too, that the power of the sun weakened, is related to the service of man.
For this is the equivalence of the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur,
that just as the atonement of Yom Kippur is accomplished through the service of man
[for although the essence of the day atones,
nevertheless,
through the service of man the atonement is with greater strength and vigor.
And moreover,
even the atonement that comes from the essence of the day is specifically when a person fulfills
(holds himself)
the essence of the day,
for the excision of the day, Yom Kippur, does not atone],
so too it is regarding the weakening of the sun's power on the fifteenth of Av
[for even after it weakened etc. there is still the sun's power,
only that its power weakened],
it is a matter related to the service of man.
